rts-1.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-1.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-1.title: Clarifying assignment feedback
rts-1.text: Your tutor has returned an assignment with a comment saying that your argument needs stronger evidence. You are unsure what kind of evidence is missing. Speak to your tutor after class, ask for clarification and arrange a practical next step.
facts: Address the tutor directly and politely.
Explain uncertainty about the comment on evidence.
Ask which claim or type of evidence needs improvement.
Suggest a specific next step such as reviewing a paragraph or attending consultation.
rts-1.sample: Excuse me, could I ask about the feedback on my assignment? You mentioned that my argument needs stronger evidence, and I would like to understand how to improve it. Is there a particular claim that needs more support, or should I use a different type of source? If you have time, could we look at one paragraph together? Otherwise, I would be happy to bring it to your next consultation session.

rts-2.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-2.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-2.title: Changing a group meeting
rts-2.text: Your group has arranged to meet tomorrow afternoon, but your work shift has unexpectedly changed. You cannot attend at that time. Speak to your group members, explain the problem and suggest a fair way to keep the project moving.
facts: Speak directly to the group and explain the scheduling conflict.
Acknowledge the inconvenience without blaming others.
Offer an alternative time or remote contribution.
Commit to completing or sharing your allocated work.
rts-2.sample: Hi everyone, I’m sorry, but my work shift has changed unexpectedly and I can’t make tomorrow afternoon’s meeting. I know we have already organised the time, so I don’t want to hold up the project. Would an evening call work for you? If not, please go ahead without me. I’ll upload my research notes beforehand and respond to any questions afterwards, so my part of the work stays on schedule.

rts-3.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-3.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-3.title: A noisy shared kitchen
rts-3.text: You share a house with other students. Recently, late-night conversations in the kitchen have made it difficult for you to sleep before morning classes. Speak to your housemates, explain the effect on you and propose a reasonable agreement.
facts: Address housemates respectfully rather than accusing them.
Explain that late kitchen conversations affect sleep before morning classes.
Make a clear, reasonable request about late-night noise.
Invite agreement or an alternative that considers everyone’s needs.
rts-3.sample: Hi everyone, could we talk about noise in the kitchen at night? I’ve been finding it difficult to sleep when conversations continue late, and I have early classes several days a week. I know the kitchen is a shared space, so I’m not asking anyone to stop using it. Could we agree to keep voices low after ten thirty, or move longer conversations elsewhere? I’m happy to discuss a time that works for everyone.

rts-4.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-4.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-4.title: Returning faulty headphones
rts-4.text: You bought headphones from a shop three days ago. One side has stopped working, although you have used them normally. You have the receipt. Speak to the shop assistant, explain the issue and ask how it can be resolved.
facts: Address the assistant politely and identify the recent purchase.
Describe the specific fault without exaggeration.
Mention normal use and that the receipt is available.
Ask for a practical resolution or assessment without inventing legal guarantees.
rts-4.sample: Hello, I bought these headphones here three days ago, and one side has already stopped working. I’ve used them normally and checked them with another device, but the problem is still there. I have the receipt with me. Could you please check the fault and explain the available options? I would prefer a working replacement if possible, but I’m happy to hear how the shop can help resolve the issue.

rts-5.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-5.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-5.title: Reporting a broken study-room projector
rts-5.text: You have booked a study room for a group presentation rehearsal this afternoon. When you arrive, the projector will not switch on. Speak to the reception staff, explain the situation and ask for help without disrupting other students’ bookings.
facts: Politely explain that the booked room’s projector will not turn on.
State the need to rehearse a group presentation this afternoon.
Ask for technical help or an available alternative room or equipment.
Respect existing bookings and consider a practical backup.
rts-5.sample: Hello, our group has booked a study room for a presentation rehearsal this afternoon, but the projector won’t switch on. Could someone check it for us? If it cannot be fixed soon, is there an available room or a portable projector we could use? We don’t want to interfere with anyone else’s booking. If there is no alternative, we can rehearse from a laptop, but working projection equipment would be very helpful.

rts-original-20261024-30.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-original-20261024-30.instruction: Read the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated and respond to the final question.
rts-original-20261024-30.title: An event runs beyond your availability
rts-original-20261024-30.text: You agreed to help at the university open day until three o'clock. The organiser has now asked you to stay until five, but you have a work shift starting at four. You want to explain your availability and offer help before leaving. What would you say to the organiser?
rts-original-20261024-30.sample: Hi, I can help until three as agreed, but I cannot stay until five because my work shift starts at four. I am happy to finish priority tasks before leaving or help hand over to someone else. Which tasks would be most useful?
facts: Communicate the purpose of the situation directly to the intended person.

rts-user-tom-book.name: Respond to a Situation
rts-user-tom-book.instruction: Read and listen to the situation. Speak directly to the person indicated, using an appropriate tone and meeting the communication goal.
rts-user-tom-book.title: Returning Tom’s book
rts-user-tom-book.text: You have to return a book to your friend, Tom, but when you get to school, you realize you have forgotten to bring it. Tom really needs it today. What will you say to Tom?
facts: Speak directly to Tom and explain that the book was forgotten.
Acknowledge that he needs it today and communicate a workable way to help.
rts-user-tom-book.sample: Hi Tom, I'm sorry, I forgot to bring your book to school, and I know you need it today. Could I go home at lunchtime and bring it back to you? If that is too late, let me know when you need it and I will try to arrange for someone to drop it off.
